verification_note: KMTC publishes one national fee structure across all campuses, so this figure does not depend on which campus you attend: Ksh 82,200 in Year 1 and Ksh 78,000 in each subsequent year for regular Kenyan students, 2025/26 structure (kmtc.ac.ke, cross-reported by Tuko, EduGuide and Education News Hub, August 2026). That was wrong, and the error is worth naming: D+ is the BIOLOGY SUBJECT requirement for this award, not the mean grade, and it had been written into the mean-grade field. KMTC publishes a minimum KCSE mean grade of C- for every certificate programme, with the cluster-subject requirement on top - for this course a D+ in Biology or Biological Sciences and a D in one of Mathematics, Chemistry, Physics or Physical Sciences. So the C- is needed overall AND the subject grades on top. The duration and the fee moved with it: the certificate runs two years rather than one, so the national schedule multiplies out to Ksh 160,200 instead of Ksh 82,200.

Kenya Utalii College is a state corporation under the Ministry of Tourism, NOT a TVET institute on the government's consolidated Ksh 67,189 rate, so that rate must not be used to derive its fees. Published Utalii figures conflict: roughly Ksh 38,850 per semester (about 77,700 a year), a quoted diploma range of Ksh 88,000-92,000, a certificate range of Ksh 80,000-85,000, and one one-year certificate quoted at Ksh 125,900. Njia will not choose among those and call the result verified, so the figure shown is an illustrative annual-equivalent scaled to course length and is flagged as such. Entry grades are from KUCCPS: a KCSE mean grade of C plain for diplomas and C- for certificates. Confirm the current fee and the exact programme list with the college or on the KUCCPS student portal before you decide. This campus opens for its pioneer intake in September 2026 with roughly 1,000 places, applications through the KUCCPS student portal at students.kuccps.ac.ke closing 23 August 2026. Six certificate programmes also run at this campus; the exact certificate list was not published in the sources available here, so confirm it on the portal rather than assuming it matches the Nairobi campus.

institution: Kenya Medical Training College (KMTC) — Kisii Campus
verification_note: KMTC publishes one national fee structure across all campuses, so this figure does not depend on which campus you attend: Ksh 82,200 in Year 1 and Ksh 78,000 in each subsequent year for regular Kenyan students, 2025/26 structure (kmtc.ac.ke, cross-reported by Tuko, EduGuide and Education News Hub, August 2026). Totals here are that schedule multiplied out by course length. Tuition only — accommodation, meals and skills-lab charges are extra and vary by campus. A non-refundable Ksh 1,500 application fee applies. Confirm with the campus before paying. Entry was previously recorded here as a D+ mean grade. That was wrong, and the error is worth naming: D+ is the BIOLOGY SUBJECT requirement for this award, not the mean grade, and it had been written into the mean-grade field. KMTC publishes a minimum KCSE mean grade of C- for every certificate programme, with the cluster-subject requirement on top - for this course a D+ in Biology or Biological Sciences and a D in one of Mathematics, Chemistry, Physics or Physical Sciences. So the C- is needed overall AND the subject grades on top. The duration and the fee moved with it: the certificate runs two years rather than one, so the national schedule multiplies out to Ksh 160,200 instead of Ksh 82,200.

ENTRY IS RECORDED AS OPEN, AND THE SOURCES CONFLICT: one states a KCSE minimum of D-, while the college's own artisan requirement is given as "a KCPE certificate or equivalent". A KCPE certificate is an ALTERNATIVE to the KCSE grade rather than an addition to it - KCPE is not marked in letter grades at all - so a learner holding an E clears the published bar. That is the same either/or already resolved this way at Sigalagala, Siaya, Kisumu, Eldoret, Kisii, Michuki and Bureti. Quoting the stricter figure would remove the card from the screen of the reader with the fewest options, who could then not even ring up to ask. Confirm with the college before travelling. Kinango TVC is a public institution and that national rate applies; it bills per term and additional mandatory charges are reported separately (hostel Ksh 4,000 per term, library Ksh 900, student activity Ksh 1,000 a year). Confirm with the registrar.

institution: Kenya Medical Training College (KMTC) — Lamu Campus
verification_note: KMTC publishes one national fee structure across all campuses, so this figure does not depend on which campus you attend: Ksh 82,200 in Year 1 and Ksh 78,000 in each subsequent year for regular Kenyan students, 2025/26 structure (kmtc.ac.ke, cross-reported by Tuko, EduGuide and Education News Hub, August 2026). Totals here are that schedule multiplied out by course length. Tuition only — accommodation, meals and skills-lab charges are extra and vary by campus. A non-refundable Ksh 1,500 application fee applies. Confirm with the campus before paying. Entry was previously recorded here as a D+ mean grade. That was wrong, and the error is worth naming: D+ is the BIOLOGY SUBJECT requirement for this award, not the mean grade, and it had been written into the mean-grade field. KMTC publishes a minimum KCSE mean grade of C- for every certificate programme, with the cluster-subject requirement on top - for this course a D+ in Biology or Biological Sciences and a D in one of Mathematics, Chemistry, Physics or Physical Sciences. So the C- is needed overall AND the subject grades on top. The duration and the fee moved with it: the certificate runs two years rather than one, so the national schedule multiplies out to Ksh 160,200 instead of Ksh 82,200.

EASA does not publish a per-course fee in any source reachable from here, only those institution-wide ranges, so no figure is shown. A midpoint of a band that spans nearly two to one is not a fee: Ksh 171,000 appears in no source, and it was displayed identically on a 36-month diploma and an 18-month one - a number a reader would budget against, against a duration it does not describe. The sentence that carried it also claimed 'the middle of the published diploma range' while the certificates showed the bottom of the IATA range instead, so the note did not describe its own records. Ring the school for the fee for your specific programme, and budget separately for accommodation at about Ksh 18,000 a month and the Ksh 1,000 application fee.

institution: Kenya Medical Training College (KMTC) — Nairobi Campus
verification_note: KMTC publishes one national fee structure across all campuses: Ksh 82,200 in Year 1 and Ksh 78,000 in each subsequent year for regular Kenyan students, 2025/26 structure (kmtc.ac.ke, cross-reported by Tuko, EduGuide and Education News Hub, August 2026). Total here is that schedule multiplied out by course length. Tuition only — accommodation, meals and skills-lab charges are extra and vary by campus. A non-refundable Ksh 1,500 application fee applies. Confirm with the campus before paying. Entry was previously recorded here as a D+ mean grade. That was wrong, and the error is worth naming: D+ is the BIOLOGY SUBJECT requirement for this award, not the mean grade, and it had been written into the mean-grade field. KMTC publishes a minimum KCSE mean grade of C- for every certificate programme, with the cluster-subject requirement on top - for this course a D+ in Biology or Biological Sciences and a D in one of Mathematics, Chemistry, Physics or Physical Sciences. So the C- is needed overall AND the subject grades on top. The duration and the fee moved with it: the certificate runs two years rather than one, so the national schedule multiplies out to Ksh 160,200 instead of Ksh 82,200.

The Kenya School of Law is a state corporation established under the Kenya School of Law Act, and this is the one programme it runs that a school leaver can enter directly - placement is through KUCCPS, which opened the May 2026 intake in February 2026. Published entry is a KCSE mean grade of C plain with at least a C+ in English or Kiswahili, so the subject grade is the real gate and a C plain alone is not enough. Alternative routes are published too: one principal pass at KACE, a pass in a certificate of law course at an accredited legal education provider, or a certificate of experiential learning from the Council of Legal Education. Two academic years minimum, three maximum. Teaching runs at the Karen campus and the Nairobi Town campus on Moi Avenue, weekday in-person days with virtual evening classes. Njia does not list the Advocates Training Programme, which is the school's better-known course: it is postgraduate and requires a law degree, so it is not a route from KCSE and listing it here would mislead. The school sets its own fees and does not publish a figure for this programme in any source reachable from this build, so it could not be verified and no figure is shown rather than a guessed one - ring the school for the current schedule.

institution: Kenya Medical Training College (KMTC) — Siaya Campus
verification_note: KMTC publishes one national fee structure across all campuses, so this figure does not depend on which campus you attend: Ksh 82,200 in Year 1 and Ksh 78,000 in each subsequent year for regular Kenyan students, 2025/26 structure (kmtc.ac.ke, cross-reported by Tuko, EduGuide and Education News Hub, August 2026). Totals here are that schedule multiplied out by course length. Tuition only — accommodation, meals and skills-lab charges are extra and vary by campus. A non-refundable Ksh 1,500 application fee applies. Confirm with the campus before paying. Entry was previously recorded here as a D+ mean grade. That was wrong, and the error is worth naming: D+ is the BIOLOGY SUBJECT requirement for this award, not the mean grade, and it had been written into the mean-grade field. KMTC publishes a minimum KCSE mean grade of C- for every certificate programme, with the cluster-subject requirement on top - for this course a D+ in Biology or Biological Sciences and a D in one of Mathematics, Chemistry, Physics or Physical Sciences. So the C- is needed overall AND the subject grades on top. The duration and the fee moved with it: the certificate runs two years rather than one, so the national schedule multiplies out to Ksh 160,200 instead of Ksh 82,200.

Programme named in Siaya National Polytechnic's published artisan course list (formerly Siaya Institute of Technology). The institution's published artisan minimum is given as a KCPE certificate or a KCSE mean grade of D-. A KCPE certificate is an alternative to the KCSE grade rather than an addition to it, so a learner holding an E clears the published bar and E is recorded. That is the same reading already applied at Kisumu, Eldoret, Kisii, Michuki and Bureti, whose published minimum has the identical shape. Recording the D- branch instead removed this course from the screen of the learner least likely to have another option, and left Siaya reading as blind to an E-grade learner while its own national polytechnic sat in the catalogue. Ask the registrar whether KCPE alone is accepted. KNEC modular courses are being phased out for CBET, so confirm which curriculum the current intake runs. Fee derived from the government's consolidated annual public-TVET fee of Ksh 67,189 (effective May 2026). Artisan fees vary more than diploma fees and published per-institution figures conflict, so treat this as an order of magnitude and confirm with the registrar.
